newsitem.title: UK: Millwall to seek administration Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: Millwall to seek administration Wednesday.

text.p: Millwall Holdings Plc, owners of English soccer club Millwall, will apply for an administration order on Wednesday, chairman Peter Mead said on Tuesday.
Mead said that the club had appointed David Buckler of Buckler Phillips as administrator to run its affairs while it grapples with a financial crisis that has left it short of cash.
Mead told Reuters that the company was seeking a "once and for all solution" to its financial problems rather than having to sell off its best players as in the past.

"The essential thing is to break out of the vicious circle," he said. When asked whether Millwall would have to sell players in the short term to tide it over its shortfall, Mead said: "I don't know. That is why David Buckler is here."
Mead would not reveal Millwall's debt level but it is thought to be just under 7.5 million pounds ($12.5 million).
He said that the club would reveal more of its refinancing plans on Wednesday but added that there had been a very encouraging initial response in talks on Tuesday.
Mead reported interest in a rights issue and said that there were other potential investors who might support the company.
Millwall shares were suspended from trading on the London Stock Exchange on Tuesday when they were valued at just 4p each.
